subjects.description: small red circular ball initially perched on the left and centre, ending on the floor at far right

observation.what_happens: A small red ball starts perched on a raised block and picture frame and falls to the brown floor, then travels to the far right side of the room. The free motion starts when it leaves its perch and ends when it comes to rest on the floor at the right.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 1525 px/s² over 1 arc = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x grows almost steadily at ~6.3 m/s while y rises to ~1.2 m near 0.5 s then falls parabolically, classic launched projectile in x-y with no circular or straight-track constraint. Constant x-speed suggests near-vacuum flight, but on Earth in air small drag should be tested. Hence vacuum vs linear vs quadratic drag compete on the unseen fall.
